text:
maria_support: Hey team — opening this thread for an escalated customer (acme-prod). They have Dedicated reserved pool ID rp-42 and are seeing sustained 429s during steady traffic bursts; customer says this violates their latency/throughput SLA. I attached sample request IDs and a small curl they used. Can infra confirm if their reserved pool is being correctly honored, or if some global rate cap is still applied? :frowning:

maria_support: Customer reported timeframe: 2026-02-17T17:20:00Z -> 17:28:00Z. Key request id examples: rq_0a1b2c, rq_0a1b2d, rq_0a1b2e. Sample response header from our API they received: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Request-Id: rq_0a1b2c
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-Dedicated-Pool: rp-42
Retry-After: 1
```

maria_support: They say client is not massively spiky — roughly 60 qps sustained, short tails to 120 qps for ~20s every minute. Their reserved pool spec (from contract): 50 qps steady with 3 concurrent burst slots. So expected behavior: short bursts should be absorbed, but they saw continuous 429s during bursts.

oncall-bot: Alert: reserved-pool-send-429s for rp-42 at 2026-02-17T17:22:11Z (severity: warning)

kevin_infra: digging in metrics now. Quick checks: are the requests actually routing to rp-42 nodes? Can you paste one full request header (obfuscated keys ok) and a request id? If X-Redwood-Dedicated-Pool is showing rp-42 on response header that's interesting — that means the request hit the pool but was still rate-limited.

maria_support: pasted rq_0a1b2d above. Full request skeleton they provided:

```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-***
X-Redwood-Project: acme-prod
Content-Length: 512
```

alex.b: a couple of hypotheses: 1) token-bucket smoothing window mismatch — their contract lists qps vs. our internal burst credit window. 2) per-route concurrency limit (model-level concurrency) hitting before pool-level capacity. 3) client is using many short connections which prevents kernel-level batching and reduces effective throughput.

alex.b: Can infra dump the pool-level token bucket counters and the per-node concurrency for rp-42 between 17:20 and 17:28? A simple query I use: 

```
SELECT time_bucket('1s', ts) AS t, sum(granted_tokens) AS tokens, sum(rejected) AS rejects
FROM pool_rate_events
WHERE pool_id = 'rp-42' AND ts >= '2026-02-17T17:20:00Z' AND ts <= '2026-02-17T17:28:00Z'
GROUP BY t ORDER BY t;
```

kevin_infra: pulled that. Summary: there were yes spikes in rejected tokens correlated with the bursts. But interestingly, total granted_tokens over window aligns with 50 qps baseline — however we see a tailing period of rejects that lasts longer than the 20s bursts. Looking at node-level, one node in rp-42 (node-07) was at 98% CPU and experiencing high latency GC pauses (we're on mixed EC2 family there). That caused its local rate limiter to temporarily deny while other nodes were healthy. We redistributed load and node-07 had degraded CPU due to unrelated background snapshot job.

sam_engineer: that matches a "fencepost" effect I've seen where the pool is sized for average qps but when a single node degrades you lose effective pool capacity and available burst slots drop unevenly. Two mitigations: 1) enable pool-level smoothing to borrow burst credits from healthy nodes, 2) avoid single-node snapshot jobs on production dedicated pools (ops).

maria_support: customer also shared a repro curl to show 429s. Asking if we can run it from our test harness to confirm behavior: 

```
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-***" \
    -H "X-Redwood-Project: acme-prod" \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.01
done
```

kevin_infra: running in staging with a mirror of rp-42 config. When I introduce a 10s CPU stall on node-07 replica in staging, I reproduce the pattern: initial burst passes, then sustained 429s even though total tokens per-second nominally available. Root cause: local node-level ratelimiter enforces per-node concurrency limits and doesn't proactively shift in-flight requests to other nodes until a connection is retried or fails. Our client retry window of 1s means many requests get 429 rather than being retried.

kevin_infra: short actionable items:
- ops: cancel snapshot job and repro on production cautiously (owner: @kevin_infra)
- infra: temporarily increase pool burst slots from 3 -> 6 for rp-42 while we stabilize (owner: @ops-team). We'll record the config change and revert after next maintenance window.
- devx: update client sdk retry behavior to exponential backoff jitter and to treat 429 with Retry-After <= 2s as retryable (owner: @alex.b).

alex.b: small client snippet suggestion (js):

```
async function requestWithRetry(req) {
  for (let i=0;i<4;i++) {
    const res = await fetch(req);
    if (res.status !== 429) return res;
    const wait = Math.min(1000 * 2 ** i, 2000) + Math.random()*100;
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, wait));
  }
  throw new Error('retry failed');
}
```

maria_support: customer asked about billing impacts — they saw no unexpected billing spikes, just failures. Can finance confirm no token-metering issue?

kevin_infra: checked metering — no anomalies. Tokens consumed were accounted as attempted, not completed; we log attempted token grant separately from billed tokens, so billing should be fine.

sam_engineer: long-term fix proposals: add cross-node preemption to shift queued requests from overloaded nodes to healthy ones, and surface pool health in Console with a "degraded nodes" alert visible to customers (so they can open tickets proactively).

maria_support: I'll communicate interim mitigation to customer: 1) increase burst slots temporarily, 2) apply client-side retry patch, 3) ops will remove snapshot job. Customer wants ETA: can we do the temporary burst bump and client SDK update today?

kevin_infra: we can bump burst slots now; will do a quick change and monitor. I set an alarm on rejects to email #support if rejects > 5% for 5m.

oncall-bot: Change applied: rp-42 burst_slots: 3 -> 6 by kevin_infra at 2026-02-17T17:30:10Z

maria_support: thanks all. Action items recap (for thread):
- kevin_infra: remove snapshot job on node-07 and monitor nodes (in progress)
- kevin_infra / ops-team: temporary bump burst slots to 6 (done)
- alex.b / devx: publish SDK patch for retry behavior and add guidance in Dedicated docs (owner: alex.b)
- sam_engineer: draft proposal for cross-node preemption + Console health indicator (owner: sam_engineer)
- finance: confirm billing unaffected (owner: finance)

maria_support: I'll update customer after we get 10m of stable metrics. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
